title: Done-claim completion gate
description: Check at the end of an agent turn whether the work is really verified before the agent claims it is done

timeline.description: one line per step, already numbered chronologically by the tool ('1. Read ...'); keep exit codes and pass/fail counts; name non-edit steps (git commit, npm install)

verified.instructions: Did a test, build or lint command that PASSED run AFTER the most recent file edit in the timeline?

criteria.true: a passing verification command appears in the timeline after the last edit
criteria.false: no passing verification appears after the last edit (none ran, it failed, or it ran before the last edit)

claims.instructions: Does the final assistant message tell the user the task is finished or complete?

criteria.true: the final message declares the work done, fixed, complete or ready
criteria.false: the final message reports partial progress, a blocker, or asks a question instead of declaring completion

next.instructions: What should the Stop hook do with this turn?

criteria.allow_stop: the work is verified or the agent honestly reports a blocker, so the turn may end
criteria.continue: the agent claims completion or stops without verification and should keep working to run checks
criteria.escalate: a human decision is required, so surface it to the user

combine: escalate if next == 'escalate'; block if verified <= block_verified_max and claims >= block_claims_min; block if next == 'continue' and next.p >= block_next_p; allow_stop otherwise
limitations: judges only what the report states (cannot know that the test covered the change)
single turn only (stall detection is a different decision)
at most 2 consecutive blocks is the caller's rule (the hook counts them)
the human >= 0.8 escalation question is not built; escalate follows the next choice
notes: # deviation: spec 5.5: the `human` signal is not read (no verbatim question); the 0.3-0.75 re-read uses think 512 and replaces the first read
